title: ORM with GORM: mapping, relationships and pitfalls

videos.script: Lesson 6 wrote every SQL statement by hand. An ORM writes them for you, from your structs. This lesson tries GORM, the most used one in Go. {{models}} Two models, an event and its tickets. GORM turns them into tables, and you will read every statement it sends. {{crud}} Then the everyday operations, one line of Go each. The log shows what each line really asked the database. {{relations}} Relationships come next. Saving an event saves its tickets. Loading them is something you ask for. {{nplus1}} Ask for them in a loop, and twenty events cost twenty-one queries. One word, Preload, brings it down to two. {{pitfalls}} Then four rules that surprise people. A zero that is not written. A delete that does not delete. {{when}} And at the end, when GORM is the right tool, and why boxoffice stays with pgx.
